events.objective: Establish symptom onset and blast radius. Determine precisely when pricing-engine p99 crossed 2s (and whether it was a step change or ramp), which services show simultaneous latency/error degradation in the same window, and the error signatures (deadline-exceeded origin: which downstream span/call is timing out). Confirm whether pricing-engine's own resource metrics (CPU, memory, GC, thread/connection pools) are saturated or normal. Report the earliest affected timestamp.

Find what changed across ALL services in the window leading up to and spanning onset. List deployments, config changes, and feature-flag changes around 2026-04-09 12:00-13:30Z for pricing-engine AND its dependencies/shared components. Map pricing-engine's service dependencies (what it calls, what calls it) to identify shared components that could explain multiple slow services. Also search historical incidents for prior 'quote latency / deadline-exceeded' patterns to find precedent.

Correlate task b's change inventory against task a's established onset time: identify the change(s) whose timestamp and affected component best align with the onset and blast radius, and name the most probable causal component (which may not be pricing-engine itself). Provide the dependency path from that component to the observed pricing-engine deadline-exceeded symptom.

redis-cache is on both the pricing-engine and market-data-service code paths, and is the only shared component in the mapped subgraph; a redis-level fault could therefore degrade both quote pricing and market data simultaneously, matching 'multiple slow services'.

events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat at ~58-66ms until the 13:20-13:22Z bucket, then jumped to >2000ms: 5-min buckets show 60.88ms avg at 13:15Z then 1370.73ms avg (max 2281.51) at 13:20Z and 2218.07ms at 13:25Z. This is a step change, not a ramp.

2-minute resolution pins onset between 13:20Z (60.87ms avg, max 61.34) and 13:22Z (2225.2ms avg, max 2227.82): last normal bucket 13:20Z, first elevated bucket 13:22Z. After peaking ~2280ms at 13:24Z the p99 decays monotonically to 1151.82ms by 14:55Z but stays >1s, i.e. it never recovered within the window.

Error signature: 192 ERROR lines in pricing-engine, all one pattern 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', first seen 13:23:57Z ('took 5171ms') and still firing at 14:58:47Z. The timing-out downstream call is market-data-service; per-call durations range 827ms-8456ms (e.g. 13:28:32Z took 8456ms).

market-data-service emits 290 WARN lines, 289 of them the single pattern 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)', first at 13:22:25Z and continuing to 14:58:22Z. Earliest quote slowdowns reported are 6864ms at 13:22:25Z. This starts ~1.5 min before pricing-engine's first ERROR and is coincident with the 13:22Z p99 step.

pricing-engine's own resources are NOT saturated: cpu_pct holds ~38-41% across 12:00-14:54Z (mean 39.83, max 44.48) with no change at onset; memory_pct holds ~48-52% (mean 49.07, max 54.93); request_rate is flat ~640 req/s (min 570.37, max 712.45) with no drop or spike. So latency rose ~2000ms with no accompanying CPU/memory/load change on pricing-engine.

Blast-radius note: the reported symptom originates in the market-data-service -> redis-cache path (cache miss storm messages name 'redis-cache' as the missing store), and all 192 pricing-engine errors attribute the timeout to market-data-service; no evidence collected of other services degrading in the window.

events.answer: pricing-engine p99 crossed 2s as a STEP change in the 13:20Z-13:22Z bucket (last normal 13:20Z at 60.87ms, first elevated 13:22Z at 2225.2ms, peak 2281.51ms at 13:24Z); earliest affected timestamp is ~13:22Z. The timeout signature is 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (first ERROR 13:23:57Z, 192 total), coincident with market-data-service's 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache' WARNs starting 13:22:25Z — i.e. the timing-out downstream call is the redis-cache-backed market-data-service snapshot rebuild. pricing-engine's own CPU (~40%), memory (~49%) and request_rate (~640 req/s) are normal and unchanged at onset, so it is not resource-saturated.

events.statement: No deployment anywhere in the quote path or org-wide in 12:00-14:00Z on 2026-04-09: get_deployments (all services) returned count 0, partial:false, and get_config_changes (all services) returned count 0, partial:false. Independently reproduced this turn, closing the partial:true caveat from the earlier all-services query.

No change on the quote path even on a widened window: deployments scoped to redis-cache for 06:00-15:00Z = count 0, and config changes scoped to redis-cache (06:00-15:00Z) and market-data-service (08:00-14:00Z) both = count 0. So the change inventory contains no candidate at all for the affected component.

redis-cache is the only shared node in the subgraph (shared:true, owner platform) and has four direct cache callers: auth-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine and market-data-service. The only deployment anywhere near the window (auth-service dep-5604 v7.2.0 11:30Z) is itself a redis-cache caller, but it landed 1h52m before the 13:22Z step and was not rolled back; no second deployment accompanies the onset.

Since the change inventory is empty, no recorded change timestamp aligns with the 13:22Z onset. The observed event that does align to the second is a cache-miss storm at the shared component: market-data-service WARN 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot' starting 13:22:25Z (289 lines), with an earliest quote slowdown of 6864ms — coincident with the 13:22Z p99 step and ~1.5 min before pricing-engine's first deadline-exceeded ERROR at 13:23:57Z.

Dependency path from the shared component to the reported symptom: redis-cache (keys quote:<n> missing) -> market-data-service rebuilds snapshot -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service (http) times out -> order-service/api-gateway trading screens show slow quotes. market-data-service also calls exchange-gateway (http), which is a downstream fallback/target of the rebuild rather than a shared component.

Precedent leads (not evidence): HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover', services redis-cache + market-data-service, symptoms 'cache miss storm','quote latency', root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', match_score 5 — matching both the component and the exact symptom wording of the live WARNs. HIST-110 (2026-01-15) shows a silent infrastructure cause (IOPS throttling) with no deployment, i.e. an empty change inventory is not proof of no infra fault.

events.answer: No deployment, config or feature-flag change aligns with the 13:22Z onset: the change inventory is empty for pricing-engine, market-data-service and redis-cache, and the only org-wide change (auth-service dep-5604 v7.2.0, 11:30Z, not rolled back) is off the quote path and 1h52m early (tc-017, tc-018, tc-022, tc-023, tc-024). The component whose event timestamp and blast radius do align is redis-cache, the only shared node in the subgraph: its miss storm ('quote:<n> not in redis-cache') starts 13:22:25Z at the same bucket as the p99 step and 1.5 min before the first deadline-exceeded ERROR (tc-019). Most probable causal component: redis-cache (quote:<n> keys missing), acting through market-data-service's snapshot rebuild -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service timeout -> trading screens (tc-019, tc-021).
